name: James Davenport
role: Supervising Faculty · Research Assistant Professor, Director of DiRAC
focus: Time-domain astronomy, magnetically active stars, optical technosignatures
bio: Research Assistant Professor in the UW Department of Astronomy and Director of the DiRAC Institute. His work centers on time-domain and large-survey astronomy — especially magnetically active stars seen by Kepler, TESS, ZTF, and Gaia — and he leads several optical SETI projects. He also directs the department's outreach efforts.

name: Anastasios Tzanidakis
focus: Giant impacts, dipper stars, circumstellar dust
bio: Studies rare stellar variability with observational and algorithmic methods — unusual dimming events around Sun-like stars, the dusty aftermath of giant impacts, and long-duration occultations by circumstellar material. Combines optical survey photometry (Gaia, ZTF, LSST) with infrared and spectroscopic follow-up. Founder of the PSI Group and former Director of the UW Planetarium.

name: Nick Tusay
bio: Works on disintegrating rocky bodies around main-sequence stars, measuring the chemical makeup of their escaping material with ground-based optical observatories and JWST. Also runs and analyzes novel radio technosignature searches with the Green Bank Telescope and the Allen Telescope Array.
